title: WPSS/1736/2007 of SMT. MUSHARRAF JAHAN Vs STATE AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
WRIT PETITION No. 1736 of 2007 (S/S)
Smt. Musharraf Jahan ---Petitioner
 Vs.
State & others --Respondents
Present :
Mr. Ramji Srivastava, Advocate, for the petitioner.
Mr. A.K. Joshi, Addl. C.S.C. for the State/respondents.

Honíble Alok Singh, J. (Oral)
 Present petition is filed assailing the order dated
22.10.2007, Annexure No.10 to the writ petition, passed
by the Additional District Inspector of Schools (Basic)
Dehradun.
 Undisputedly, vide Advertisement dated 19.09.2004,
applications were invited for the post of Assistant Teacher
(Urdu) from those who on 01.07.2001 were in the age
group of 18 years to 35 years and were having Graduation
Degree or Equivalent thereto alongwith Urdu subject and
were also having B.T.C. Certificate and were having
Moallim-E-Urdu prior to 11.08.1997, thereafter, vide
corrigendum, maximum age was increased from 35 years
to 50 years. Petitioner applied within time alongwith all
requisite documents and was declared successful and an
appointment letter was also issued in favour of the
petitioner on 14.12.2004. Petitioner gave her joining in
Primary School, Rampur Khurd, Sahaspur, District
Dehradun.
 Writ Petition No. 1397 of 2004 (S/S) was preferred
before this Court by Mohd. Shaleem and others. Writ
petition, so filed, was disposed of by the learned Single
Judge of this Court vide judgment dated 08.03.2006.
Learned Single Judge of this Court vide judgment dated

2
08.03.2006 was pleased to direct the Secretary,
Education, Uttarakhand to hold inquiry into the entire
selection process. Pursuant to the judgment dated
08.03.2006, inquiry was held and vide order dated
22.10.2007, appointment of the petitioner as well as four
others were cancelled/revoked saying that the selection
and appointment of the petitioner and others was in
violation of Uttar Pradesh Basic Education (Teachers)
Service Rules, 1981 as amended in 1998. Feeling
aggrieved, petitioner has approached this Court by way of
present petition.
 I have heard Mr. Ramji Srivastava, learned counsel
appearing for the petitioner and Mr. A.K. Joshi, Addl.
C.S.C. appearing for the State/respondents and have
carefully perused the record.
Rule 8 of the Rules 1981 as amended in the year
1998, reads as under.

(4) The essential qualification of candidates for
appointment to the posts referred to in clause (a) and
sub-clause (iii) and (iv) of clause (b) of Rule 5 for teaching
Urdu Language shall be as follows:
(i) A Bachelor's Degree from a University established by
law in India or a Degree recognized by the Government as
equivalent thereto with Urdu as one of the subjects.
 Note:- A candidate who does not possess the
aforesaid qualification in Urdu, shall be eligible for
appointment, if he possesses a Master's Degree in Urdu.
(ii) Basic Teacher's Certificate from any of the training
centers in Lucknow, Agra, Mawana in district Meerut and
Sakaldiha in district Chandauli established by the

5
any other training qualification recognized by the
Government as equivalent thereto."
As per sub-Rule (4) of Rule 8 of the Rules of 1981, as
amended in 1998, for the post of Assistant Teacher Urdu
requisite qualification is:
 A bachelor degree from a University established by
law in India or a degree recognized by the Government as
equivalent thereto with Urdu as one of the subject. If a
candidate does not possess the aforesaid qualification in
Urdu shall be eligible for the appointment, if he possesses
a master degree in Urdu. Rule further provides that
candidate must possess Basic Teachers Certificate from
any of the training centers in Lucknow, Agra, Mawana in
District Meerut and Sakaldiha in District Chandauli
established by the Government for imparting training for
teaching Urdu or any other training qualification
equivalent thereto.
Meaning thereby, a candidate seeking appointment
on the post of Assistant Teacher (Urdu) should either
have B.A. or equivalent degree with Urdu subject or
master degree in Urdu and B.T.C. certificate or equivalent
certificate issued by the different centers mentioned
therein.
Perusal of Government Order dated 13.09.1994,
Annexure No. 11 to the writ petition, would reveal that for
the post of Assistant Teacher in Junior/Senior Basic
School, Examination Certificate of Adib-E-Mahir issued
by Urdu Academy, Aligarh shall be equivalent to
Intermediate examination, while Adib-E- Kamil
Examination Certificate shall be equivalent to B.A.
(Graduation with Urdu subject).

6
Section 87 and 2 (f) of U.P. Re-Organization Act,
2000, are being reproduced herein:-
87. ìPower to adapt laws.-For the purpose of
facilitating the application in relation to the
State of Uttar Pradesh or Uttaranchal of any
law made before the appointed day, the
appropriate Government may, before the
expiration of two years from that day, by order,
make such adaptations and modifications of
the law, whether by way of repeal or
amendment, as may be necessary or expedient,
and thereupon every such law shall have effect
subject to the adaptations and modifications so
made until altered, repealed or amended by a
competent Legislature or other competent
authority.
Explanation.- In this section, the expression
"appropriate Government" means as respects
any law relating to a matter enumerated in the
Union List, the Central Government, and as
respects any other law in its application to a
State, the State Government.î
2(f) "law" includes any enactment, ordinance,
regulation, order, bye-law, rule, scheme, notification
or other instrument having, immediately before the
appointed day, the force of law in the whole or in
any part of the existing State of Uttar Pradesh.
Perusal of Section 87 read with sub-Section (f) of
Section 2 of the Act would reveal that any law or
notification or Government Order enacted or issued by
the State of Uttar Pradesh prior to the appointed day and
was in existence as on appointed day shall be deemed
having force of law within territory of the State of
Uttarakhand even after the appointed day till same is
modified or altered or repealed by the State of
Uttarakhand.
Mr. A.K. Joshi, learned Addl. C.S.C. appearing for
the State does not dispute that Government Order dated
13.09.1994, as referred above, has never been repealed,
superseded or recalled.

7
 Perusal of the Annexure No. 3 to the writ petition
would reveal that petitioner did High School in 1975 with
Urdu as one of the subject, Intermediate in 1978 with
Urdu as one of the subject and did Adib-E- Kamil from
Jamiyan Urdu Aligarh, thereafter, M.A. from Meerut
University in the year 1983 and B.Ed. in 1984. Page
No. 29 of the paper book would reveal that petitioner also
did Moilim-E- Urdu training from Jamiyan Urdu Aligarh.
 It is also not in dispute that at the time of filing the
application for the post pursuant to the advertisement,
petitioner was within the age group as required by the
advertisement and the petitioner was declared successful
and was given appointment.
 Since, petitioner was having all the requisite
qualifications and was declared successful, therefore,
petitionerís appointment seems to have been wrongly
revoked on the ground that selection and appointment of
the petitioner alongwith others was in violation of Rules of
1981 as amended in 1998.
 Consequently, impugned order does not sustain in
law and is hereby quashed. Writ petition is allowed.
Petitioner is reinstated to its post. Since, petitionerís
appointment was cancelled for no fault of the petitioner
and petitioner was made to suffer by an illegal order
dated 22.10.2007, therefore, petitioner shall be entitled
for all consequential benefits.
(Alok Singh, J.)
 30.03.2015
JM/Deepak
